name: 3B Blackbio DX Ltd
tagline: Debt-free, high-margin (~78% MDx EBITDA, 25% ROCE) Indian molecular-diagnostics niche compounder, but headline growth is acquisition-inflated -- the organic core has decelerated to mid-teens and Coris is a near-term drag
business_overview: 3B Blackbio DX (formerly Kilpest India, BSE 532067; renamed Aug 2023 after merging in subsidiary 3B BlackBio Biotech) makes and exports PCR-based molecular-diagnostic kits, enzymes and reagents (TRUPCR/TRURAPID/TRUNGS/TRUdPCR, 120+ assays), plus a small retained agrochemical/biopesticide business. It has expanded into Europe/AMR via TRUPCR Europe Ltd (UK) and the Aug-2025 acquisition of Coris BioConcept (Belgium, rapid lateral-flow AMR tests).

FY24 Rs 32cr -> FY25 Rs 48cr -> FY26 Rs 60cr; Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 9.0cr, -29% YoY (Coris H1 loss); organic ex-Coris PAT +8.2%
~40.95%, stable (Dubey family; low for a promoter-run company but not falling)
fundamentals_narrative: Deep read (FY26 AR/concall + Q1 FY27 results + concall) shows a genuinely high-quality organic core wrapped in acquisition-inflated headline numbers. FY26 consolidated revenue rose 47%, but ~two-thirds of that was the Coris BioConcept consolidation (from 29-Aug-2025, adding Rs 35.9cr revenue and Rs 8.8cr PAT in a partial, H2-weighted year); organic India molecular diagnostics grew only ~10% (Rs 78.3cr -> Rs 86.5cr). Q1 FY27 makes the split explicit: consolidated revenue +50.6% but PAT -29% YoY, entirely because Coris is seasonally loss-making in Q1/Q2 (Q1 FY27 Coris EBITDA -EUR 325K) and only turns profitable in H2 on HAT-order supply timing. Strip Coris out and the organic business grew revenue +11.8% and PAT +8.2%, with MDx EBITDA margin ~78% -- structurally excellent economics, debt-free, ROCE ~25%, clean cash conversion (CFO/PAT ~0.87). Exports grew 38% but management repeatedly cites geopolitical headwinds delaying/cancelling orders. FY27 guidance is 15-20% consolidated revenue growth, with Coris guided to '10-15% sales growth and slight positive EBITDA' for the full year -- i.e. the acquisition is a turnaround/optionality bet, not yet an accretive bolt-on. Real optionality sits further out: US FDA registration for Coris's RESIST-5 AMR panel (1-2 years, US market 2027-28) and IVDR certification (BSI notified body; legacy CE-IVD sales allowed to Dec-2028). Promoter holding is low (~41%) but stable.

bull_case: Organic core economics are outstanding: ~78% MDx EBITDA margin, ~25% ROCE, ~19.8% ROE, effectively debt-free, CFO/PAT ~0.87 -- an IP-heavy assay portfolio (120+ assays) on a reagent-rental razor/blade model with 15+ long-term (2-3yr) contracts
Small base (~Rs 1,245 Cr market cap) vs an ~10x-larger unlisted leader (Molbio); molecular diagnostics adoption in India is structurally growing and 3B runs higher margins than Molbio
Genuine multi-year optionality: US FDA registration for Coris's RESIST-5 AMR panel (US market 2027-28), IVDR certification progressing, and new higher-margin panels (oncology, respiratory)
Coris is seasonally loss-making only in H1; H2 HAT-order timing swings it to profit, and full-year FY27 is guided to slight positive EBITDA -- a drag that should ease
bear_case: Headline growth is acquisition-inflated: FY26 +47% consolidated vs organic India MDx ~+10%; Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue +50% but PAT -29% YoY -- the organic core has decelerated to mid-teens

Coris is currently a drag, not an accretive bolt-on: Q1 FY27 EBITDA -EUR 325K, 'seasonally loss-making in Q1 and Q2', full-year only 'slight positive EBITDA' guided -- it is a turnaround/optionality bet
Valuation (~22x P/E, ~3.8x P/B) already reflects the quality and roughly matches the 15-20% guide; little embedded upside unless US FDA / IVDR / Coris deliver, none of which is in FY27 numbers
Export growth repeatedly attributed to 'geopolitical headwinds'; promoter holding low at ~41%; operating leverage in the organic core is largely exhausted at ~78% EBITDA margin
verdict_headline: High-quality niche compounder with real long-runway optionality, but the near-term inflection isn't there -- organic growth has slowed to mid-teens and Coris drags FY27; Medium, not Medium-High
verdict_reasoning: The organic business is genuinely excellent -- ~78% MDx EBITDA margin, ~25% ROCE, debt-free, clean cash conversion -- and the small base vs Molbio plus US FDA / IVDR optionality fit a long-horizon (100x-in-10-years) compounding profile better than a near-term 10x

But the deep read is a modest negative vs the prior write-up: the '29%/47% growth' was acquisition-driven, organic India MDx grew only ~10% in FY26 and organic PAT +8% in Q1 FY27, and reported consolidated PAT actually fell 29% YoY on the Coris H1 loss

Conviction cut to Medium (from Medium-High; not floor-forced): quality and optionality are real, but there is no live earnings inflection to underwrite, valuation is full at ~22x, and the FY27 story leans on an unproven Coris turnaround
